subject: psychology
title: Issues & Debates: Free Will, Determinism, Nature & Nurture
welcome_lead: Are we free, predetermined, born or built? Classic debates with modern evidence.
meta_desc: A-Level Psychology debates: free will vs determinism, nature vs nurture, interactionism.
final_note: Most modern psychology lands on interactionism — but degree matters.

concepts.def: All behaviour fully caused by internal/external forces.
Behaviour caused but allows some conscious choice (James).
We choose our actions independent of biological/social causes.
Innate, genetic, biological influences on behaviour.
Environmental and learned influences on behaviour.

walkthroughs.body_html: Hard determinism denies free will entirely — behaviourism, biological approach. Soft determinism (William James) allows conscious choice within causal limits. Libet (1985) showed brain activity precedes conscious decision by ~300ms — fuelling the determinism case.

The debate stretches from Descartes (nature) to Locke (nurture as blank slate). Modern psychology uses heritability coefficients: IQ heritability is ~0.5. Epigenetics shows environment switches genes on or off — the divide is mostly false.

Diathesis-stress: genetic vulnerability + environmental stressor produces disorders like schizophrenia. Plomin's three gene-environment relationships — passive, evocative, active — show nature and nurture are entangled rather than opposed.
